scope: Shared Work additional duration, Koodo book totals and Mihon chapter totals

checks.name: Koodo recorded seconds convert exactly to milliseconds
Explicit zero remains an adoptable duration
Fractional source seconds are rejected
Negative source seconds are rejected
Boolean is not coerced into a duration
Unit conversion must remain a safe integer
Missing source bucket remains unknown
Overlapping daily view is not added to the cumulative value
Selected books mapped to one Work are aggregated before adoption
Repeated identical source key contributes only once
Conflicting duplicate source key blocks the duration
Conflicting target for one source key is not silently chosen
Aggregation overflow is rejected
Existing additional duration is preserved by default
Source ten hours minus three hours of activity sets seven hours
Old additional value is replaced rather than incremented
Repeated explicit adoption does not add another source total
New activity after adoption remains independently counted
New explicit adoption uses its new activity baseline
Smaller source total preserves records instead of clamping
Explicit zero may clear an additional value when no activity exists
Unknown source total cannot clear the existing value
Changed additional baseline reports conflict
New Work adopts a total as its initial additional duration
State, completions and resume position are unaffected
Preparing adoption does not mutate its input record
Mihon chapter totals retain their source millisecond unit
Cleared last-read date does not discard cumulative time
Repeated chapter history is not counted twice
Both declared Mihon and Tachiyomi models expose readDuration
64-bit duration above the native safe range is rejected
Absent history supplies no inferred zero total
All synthetic source inputs remain unchanged

limits: These are explicit adoption models, not production database operations.
Existing SQLite, protobuf and PDF probes remain separate evidence.
UI, concurrent persistence and all four native Work branches require implementation acceptance.
